For businesses in deregulated energy markets, learning the difference between the utility and an energy supplier is an important part of evaluating energy options. While both play important roles in delivering energy to your business, their responsibilities are different. Understanding how their roles differ can simplify energy decisions and provide greater confidence when reviewing plans, agreements, and evaluating your options.


Looking for a quick visual overview?[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/1219883813) to learn how each entity supports your energy service.


**The Role of the Utility**


The utility is responsible for delivering electricity or natural gas to your business. Electric utilities own and maintain the poles, wires, and other equipment that bring power to your facility. Utilities are also responsible for reading meters, responding to outages and emergencies, maintaining the infrastructure, and providing your energy bill.


If your business experiences a power outage, a downed power line, or another service-related issue, the utility is responsible for restoration.


**The Role of an Energy Supplier**


An energy supplier, like AEP Energy, manages the generation, or supply, portion of your energy service. Energy suppliers purchase electricity or natural gas from wholesale markets and offer competitive plans to homes and businesses in deregulated energy markets.


Depending on your location, businesses may have the opportunity to choose their energy supplier and evaluate a variety of plan options, contract terms, and pricing structures. Energy choice gives businesses the ability to compare options and select a solution that aligns with their needs and priorities.


An energy supplier can help with:


- Plan selection and enrollment
- Contract renewals
- Account questions and support
- Understanding available energy products
- Evaluating options based on goals and budgets


Choosing an energy supplier does not change how energy is delivered to your business. The utility continues to deliver electricity or natural gas through the same system that serves your location. There are no equipment changes and no service interruptions.


**AEP Energy Supports Small Businesses**


As a competitive energy supplier, AEP Energy helps small businesses navigate their energy options with solutions designed to fit a variety of operational needs and budget goals.


Whether you’re exploring energy choice for the first time, reviewing an upcoming renewal, or looking for a trusted energy partner, our Small Business Consultants can help you evaluate available options. With personalized support and industry expertise, we work to simplify the energy purchasing process so you can stay focused on running your business.
